# Phylogenetics Tree Metrics

Match the requested metric to its biological input object and observation unit.

## Input And Metric

- Branch-length sums, patristic distances, and long-branch metrics require
  phylogenetic trees with the relevant branch lengths and rooting assumptions.
- Informative-site, composition-variability, alignment-length, and gap metrics
  require multiple sequence alignments. A FASTA suffix alone does not prove the
  sequences are aligned.

Publication link: https://academic.oup.com/bioinformatics/article-abstract/37/16/2325/6131675

Calculate RCV (relative composition variability) for an alignment.

Lower RCV values are thought to be desirable because they represent
a lower composition bias in an alignment. Statistically, RCV describes
the average variability in sequence composition among taxa. 

RCV is calculated following Phillips and Penny, Molecular Phylogenetics
and Evolution (2003), doi: 10.1016/S1055-7903(03)00057-5.

Aliases: 
  relative_composition_variability, rel_co

def rcv(path):
    p=subprocess.run(['.venv/bin/phykit','rcv',str(path),'--json'], text=True, capture_output=True, check=True)
    return float(json.loads(p.stdout)['rcv'])

    vals=[]

    {'alternative':'less','method':'asymptotic'},
    {'alternative':'greater','method':'asymptotic'},
]:

# Recompute common subset only; this is a sensitivity check, not changing the selected all-archive analysis.

for i,k in enumerate(common,1):
    a.append(rcv(A[k])); f.append(rcv(F[k]))

res=mannwhitneyu(a,f,alternative='two-sided',method='asymptotic')
